details.label: Discussion
details.text: Developing/agitated cumulus are noted underneath an upper-level cirrus canopy as of 1830 UTC via recent satellite imagery. Aided by weak forcing for ascent associated with a subtle mid-level perturbation progressing quickly eastward out of southern Ontario, continued insolation to the south of a weak surface cold front is expected to support isolated to widely scattered thunderstorm development over the next 1-3 hours. Effective shear of 30-35 kts and around 1000-1500 J/kg MLCAPE will promote some potential for a few stronger updrafts. Water-loaded downbursts capable of isolated damaging wind gusts will be possible with these more robust updrafts given modestly steep low-level lapse rates and a corridor of locally greater PW (1.5-1.75"). An instance of marginally severe hail also cannot be ruled out with any transient supercell structure that can develop. Weak mid-level lapse rates should largely temper overall convective intensity and severe coverage, however. Thus, watch issuance is not anticipated at this time

details.label: Discussion
details.text: An ongoing MCS currently extending across portions of southern West Virginia has largely waned in intensity over the past 1-2 hours with modest cloud top warming noted via recent satellite imagery. In addition, a gradual transition toward a more outflow-dominant storm mode is likely ongoing as convection continues to encounter a more weakly sheared environment with southeastward extent (effective shear of 20 kts or less noted across western Virginia and northern North Carolina via latest objective analysis). Regardless, expectation is for this activity to continue south-southeastward through this afternoon along a surface buoyancy gradient. Modestly steeper low-level lapse rates noted downstream across the Piedmont should allow at least some potential for damaging wind gusts to continue, with the greatest potential likely to reside with the convection located along the aforementioned instability gradient. This threat is expected to remain generally isolated, however, owing to the more weakly sheared environment. Trends will continue to be monitored, but a downstream watch appears unlikely at this time

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent KIND base velocity data suggest a strengthening cold pool with ongoing storms over Boone, Hamilton, and Madison Counties, to the north of the Indianapolis metropolitan area. That convection is located near an outflow/warm front composite boundary that has become better defined early this afternoon from central into southeast IN. The air mass to the west of the boundary continues to destabilize with latest objective analysis indicating MLCAPE as high as 3000 J/kg. While low-level lapse rates remain somewhat marginal, continued daytime heating ahead of the ongoing storms should support a steepening trend through the afternoon. The current KIND VWP is sampling largely westerly deep-layer flow with 40-45 kt of deep-layer shear. While the shear vector orientation is not ideally aligned with the ongoing storms as of present, the upstream KLOT VWP suggests that the shear vector may become more favorably oriented with time. When combined with the destabilizing inflow air mass, the setup appears favorable for a corridor of enhanced damaging wind potential focused along or just to the north of the composite boundary
